summary.headline: Sagar Cements Q1 FY27: volumes up ~13% YoY but loss after tax of ₹28 crore and EBITDA of ₹451/tonne on West Asia-driven cost inflation.
summary.overview: Volumes grew about 13% YoY and revenue rose 5% YoY, with realisations broadly stable. Profitability moderated as energy, fuel and packaging costs rose amid West Asia tensions, leaving EBITDA at ₹451 per tonne and a loss after tax of ₹28 crore. Management maintained a 7 million tonne volume target for FY27 (excluding clinker) and reiterated FY27 EBITDA guidance of ₹500–550 per tonne, down from the earlier ~₹600 reference raised by an analyst. Capex completed in the quarter includes Jeerabad 0.5 million tonne expansion and the remaining 1.55 MW of Gudipadu waste heat recovery; the 0.75 million tonne Andhra Cements expansion is expected by quarter-end.

segments.name: Mattampally (Telangana)
segments.commentary: Utilisation 65% in Q1; debt-free per management and carries waste heat recovery, which keeps its grid power cost lower.

segments.name: Gudipadu (AP)
segments.commentary: Utilisation 79% in Q1; remaining 1.55 MW of the 4.35 MW waste heat recovery commissioned, with ~₹25/tonne consolidated saving expected.

segments.name: Jeerabad (MP)
segments.commentary: Utilisation 96% in Q1; 0.5 million tonne expansion completed, with ramp-up expected as soon as possible and some clinker still sold until volumes stabilise.

segments.name: Andhra Cements
segments.commentary: Utilisation near 50%, targeted at ~60% by end-FY27 and 60–70% thereafter; variable cost ~₹100–125/tonne above Mattampally due to grid power with no waste heat recovery; new cement mill due end-September.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target of ~7 million tonnes, excluding clinker sales; management sees FY28 volume growth in double digits.
FY27 EBITDA guidance of ₹500–550 per tonne, assuming prices stay flat; management said ₹550 is 'definitely doable'.
Q2 FY27 to see cost increase from maintenance shutdowns at three plants (Mattampally, Jeerabad among them) and inventory cost adjustment; management expects recovery in Q3 and Q4.
Management pencilled in ~₹100/tonne cost inflation (₹50 power and fuel, ₹50 miscellaneous), offset by efficiency gains; inventory covers operations up to mid-October.
No capex plans beyond ~₹30–40 crore annual maintenance through 2028, apart from ~₹240 crore of ongoing capex spread over FY27 and FY28.
Vizag land monetisation of ₹150 crore pencilled for FY27 and ~₹200 crore for FY28, pending a generic Government GO.
capex_capacity: Jeerabad 0.5 million tonne capacity expansion completed in Q1; Madhya Pradesh volumes expected to rise after this.
Gudipadu 1.55 MW waste heat recovery commissioned, completing 4.35 MW total installed capacity.
Andhra Cements 0.75 million tonne cement capacity expansion expected to complete before end of Q2 FY27.
New cement mill at Andhra due for commissioning end-September 2026.
Andhra waste heat recovery planned in the next couple of years, expected to deliver savings similar to Gudipadu's.
Super fine building material work has started; operational plan to be shared by end of Q2.
demand_pricing: South footprint ~80% of volumes; AP and Telangana combined Q1 demand up ~11% YoY, Tamil Nadu ~4% (April negative, June ~20%), Kerala ~12%, Karnataka flat; South demand ~6–6.5% YTD, expected at 8–10% for FY27.
Madhya Pradesh demand grew ~9–10%; Maharashtra and Odisha described as healthy.
July demand expected to track Q1 trend, with labour availability back.
Prices rose early in Q1 but moderated late in the quarter; flat from March exit to July, with a ₹50–60/tonne realisation gain cited.
Management expects price hikes eventually, citing flat cement inflation over 10 years against substantial cost inflation; timing and size uncertain amid competitive intensity.
Tamil Nadu ban on transport of rough stones and aggregates to other states: management sees no impact.
Heat waves and election-related labour shortages in Eastern and Southern India disrupted Q1 execution.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7 million tonne FY27 volume target ex-clinker, and how much clinker will be sold in Q2 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: The 7 mt target excludes clinker. Clinker is still sold to Andhra Cements' sister unit Bayyavaram and some outside, and some at Jeerabad until ramp-up; management would not quantify volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Is double-digit volume growth possible in FY28, and what is the Q2 cost inflation and is the ~₹600/t EBITDA guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says FY27 and FY28 both see double-digit volume growth. Full-year cost pressure is about ₹100/t across fuel, raw material and miscellaneous, offset by savings; Q2 gets extra inventory and maintenance cost at three plants. Guidance is ₹500–550/t, assuming flat prices, not ~₹600.

qa_highlights.question: Are prices stable versus Q1 averages?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices have been flat from March exit to July and June to July; realisation was up about ₹50–60/t, with the cause unclear (mix or price hikes).

qa_highlights.question: Status of Vizag land sale and FY27 realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Awaiting a generic Government GO after the government signalled it would replace a case-specific order; the ₹150 crore for FY27 is still seen as doable. Management said buyer engagement exists but timelines were the issue.

qa_highlights.question: Which regions drive incremental H2 FY27 demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Almost all incremental volume comes from the South (~80% of footprint). Madpradesh is also expected to rise after the 0.5 mt Jeerabad expansion, supporting the ~15% growth projected for the year.

qa_highlights.question: How does Andhra Cements' cost structure compare with Mattampally, and how should the three units be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Variable cost at Andhra is ₹100–125/t higher than Mattampally because it buys grid power without waste heat recovery; management says the kcal and unit metrics are at par. Andhra carries most of the debt, and management offered to share modelling details offline.

qa_highlights.question: Can Q1 EBITDA of ~₹425/t reach ₹600/t for full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ₹550/t is 'definitely doable', citing Gudipadu WHR savings, Jeerabad expansion and the Andhra cement mill due end-September, assuming stable prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is capex going to rise, and what is the debt reduction path?
qa_highlights.answer: No new capex beyond ₹30–40 crore annual maintenance through 2028. About ₹240 crore of ongoing capex spreads over FY27 and FY28; operating cash flow is not yet reflected in the gross debt path.

qa_highlights.question: What are the levers to manage power and fuel costs if the West Asia crisis escalates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has no control over prices and can only manage consumption, which it says is efficient. Inventory covers operations to mid-October; ₹100/t inflation is pencilled in (₹50 fuel, ₹50 other), and clinker is at its peak.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the Tamil Nadu ban on rough stone and aggregate transport, and what limestone auction premiums are seen?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no impact. Recent Telangana limestone auctions, about a year or 18 months old, went at 50–75% premiums; other auctions are pending in TN, AP and Telangana.

qa_highlights.question: Will the land sale and volume ramp support the net debt projection?
qa_highlights.answer: Parth Bhavsar asked about net debt trajectory. Management said the ₹150 crore land sale is in FY27 and about ₹200 crore in FY28.

risks_watch: Cost pressure: ~₹100/t FY27 inflation pencilled in, with clinker at peak; inventory covers operations only up to mid-October, and Q2 faces extra inventory and maintenance cost at Mattampally and Jeerabad.
Guidance credibility: FY27 EBITDA guidance of ₹500–550/t depends on flat prices, cost savings from Gudipadu WHR, Jeerabad ramp-up and the Andhra mill (end-September); Q1 was ₹451/t.
Pricing: realisation gains of ₹50–60/t are not attributed; management says a price hike is needed eventually but timing and size are uncertain given competitive intensity.
Vizag land monetisation (₹150 crore FY27, ~₹200 crore FY28) still awaits a generic Government GO, and the buyer timeline is unclear.
Debt: gross debt ₹1,704 crore and D/E 0.78:1; the operating cash flow debt reduction is not yet in the plan, and ~₹240 crore of ongoing capex runs through FY28.
Andhra Cements: utilisation near 50% vs ~60% target by end-FY27, with grid-power cost ₹100–125/t above Mattampally until its waste heat recovery is built in the next couple of years.
key_quotes: We remain confident of achieving volumes of approximately 7 million tons in FY 2027, supported by our expanding market presence and ongoing operational initiatives.
What we have indicated and what we remain committed is around ₹500 to ₹550 EBITDA per tonne.
₹550 is definitely doable, as I mentioned to you.
I don't think we have ability to control the inflation. We only have ability to control the quantity of usage.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on volume (7 mt FY27, double-digit growth in FY28) and on the ₹500–550/t EBITDA guidance, but cautious on near-term costs and pricing. Answers on the Vizag GO, Andhra cost modelling and clinker volumes were less specific, with some items deferred to offline discussion.
